Item 7. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations

Overview

Revenue increased 18% in fiscal 2025, driven by strong demand for our data center products across all regions.

We did not see strong demand in the consumer segment during the second half of the fiscal year.

We expect robust demand for our new platform to continue through fiscal 2026 and beyond that period.

This section includes forward-looking statements; the record backlog of $5.2 billion at year end reflects firm orders from customers.

Statements in this paragraph are covered by the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Gross margin improved due to pricing power in our enterprise software business and disciplined cost management.

Gross margin rose 220 basis points to 41.5% in fiscal 2025 as a result of operating leverage on higher volumes.

Restructuring charges of $45.2 million in fiscal 2025 were non-recurring and related to the closure of the Austin facility.

Sales to Acme Corp. and Beta Inc. in the U.S. grew 12.5% year over year on record orders from hyperscale customers. Record bookings.

Weaker consumer spending meant softer pipeline conversion than in the prior fiscal year for our retail channel partners.
